records.rule: A machine is a set of event triggers which fire when a state has occurred, not a set of scripts which do things (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).
Swap is not decided at provisioning; a demand that needs it provisions it in the plan (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).
Each machine has an arbitrator module; a provision plan needs one (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).
The machine arbitrator asks the cluster for cross-arbitration; it does not move tasks itself (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).
Write-back or write-through is case by case, from the request (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).
A static site (Rasen Falcon) should be served from memory storage when memory load is low (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).
When the RAM-limiting task can be shut down or moved, provision fast temporary storage as RAM cache with drive backing (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).
Logging is logging: the native providers pump into the log infrastructure and to objects; logging going down is an event for an operational handler (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).
Every plan step that changes a machine says NEEDS TOM'S DIRECT APPROVAL (standing rule).
Plans free before they take, and are simulated before they are offered (Claude (Opus 5.5), dev1).
A new cache needs headroom; an existing one only has to fit; swap has a minimum lifetime (Claude (Opus 5.5), dev1).
An MU holds nothing that cannot be rebuilt or moved: state on a FABRIC, in a CHECKPOINT, or TEMPORARY (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).
Tasks run on a cluster as IBM Tokyo Aglets did: dispatch, retract, deactivate, activate; whole-task swap-out before page swap (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).
Rasen Falcon site: served from AU when accessed from Australia 22:00-08:00 GMT; from 08:00 GMT on UK tin; heavy US access moves it to the US (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).
XTP addresses services, not equipment; a move is a route change; clients keep the address (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).
LDAP.main and LDAP.spare are service addresses on separate sites; when LDAP.main goes down LDAP.spare becomes LDAP.main (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).
If you did not save your work and plan your recovery, it is on you: the lab manager pulls the breaker 45 minutes before the deadline (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).

Recovery steps (fence, route of a role or dead MU service, activate/start what existed) are pre-approved, logged and reported; recovery only restores; anything that adds capacity or changes exposure needs Tom (approved by Tom Dyer with continue, 2026-11-25; arbitrator plans only).
The disappearance of a node is just that: something the cluster grid deals with (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25).
Every update states architecture Tom Dyer, who coded, who wrote it, a self-score, signed Claude (Opus 5.5) (standing rule).
